newsitem.title: INDIA: Multinational stocks lead charge in Bombay rally.
newsitem.headline: Multinational stocks lead charge in Bombay rally.

text.p: ** (0730 GMT) - Shares rally strongly in afternoon trade;
Bombay share index up 52.28 points, or 1.25 percent, at
** Multinational stocks lead charge on increased foreign
and local fund buying, dealers say
** Monsoon session of India's parliament gets off to noisy
start, upper house adjourns over lawmakers' angry
demands for dimissal of two regional governments
** National exchange index gains 24.45 pts at 1,197.70 at

Renewed foreign fund buying in multinational stocks dominated action in Bombay shares on Wednesday, with a smart rally from blue chips pushing the index up over one percent in early afteroon trade, traders said.
"There is a lot of demand for fast-moving consumer goods stocks (FMCG) such as Hindustan Lever, Nestle and Colgate," said Sanjeev Choithani, chief dealer at local brokers Pashupati Advani.
Market participants said newspaper reports that the U.S.'s Alliance Capital planned to float a $60-million offshore fund targeting Indian FMCG stocks led to renewed action in these shares.
Alliance officials in Bombay were not immediately available for comment.

The Economic Times newspaper on Wednesday said roadshows for Alliance's $60-million offshore fund aimed at capitalising on rising interest among foreign institutional investors (FIIs) in FMCG stocks, brand-driven companies and multinational companies had already begun.
Shares of Colgate rose 9.25 rupees at 314.50, Nestle gained 7.25 rupees at 294.50 and Hindustan Lever added 27.20 at 1,363.0.
Among other individual stocks, petrochemicals giant Reliance Industries jumped 10.0 rupees, or nearly three percent, boosted by news the firm has raised prices of its key product, brokers said.
Trade sources said Reliance has raised polyester filament yarn to 71,000 rupees per tonne from 68,000 rupees.
